trust_decision.summary: Caller-supplied url and accept header strings are matched by regexes in parse() and extractUrlVariableNames() on the assumption that they are well-formed; three of those regexes backtrack polynomially on crafted input (ReDoS).

landing_point.why: Advisory title says 'Regular Expression in parse'; the preview-extraction regex on headers.accept in parse() is the first regex a reader meets there.

fix_sites.entry_point: endpoint(route, options) / endpoint.parse(options) with url ending /graphql and mediaType.previews set (src/endpoint-with-defaults.ts:12, src/with-defaults.ts:22)
endpoint(route, options) / endpoint.parse(options), called from src/parse.ts:30 on the url template
same as above, removeNonChars applied to each match

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/util/extract-url-variable-names.ts:1-4 is a helper called directly by parse() at src/parse.ts:30, one hop from the landing point, not a separate implementation

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue the URL is developer-controlled route text, not attacker input, so only the accept-header regex at src/parse.ts:62 matters.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Previews already present in the accept header (e.g. 'application/vnd.github.foo-preview+json') must still be extracted and merged with mediaType.previews; URL variables like {owner}, {+path}, {?q,page} must still be extracted so they are omitted from body/query.

O6_input_shapes: accept header: long run of [\w-] characters without a '-preview' suffix (fix.diff:13-14)
url: long run of '{' without a closing '}' (fix.diff:23-24)
url variable expression: long run of non-word characters not at end of string (fix.diff:27-28)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the mediaType.format rewrite regex on each accept part could realistically be written with nested/overlapping quantifiers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it already parses the same untrusted accept header with optional groups; a maintainer extending it to more vendor formats could write an ambiguous pattern

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the template tokeniser regex could be written as /\{([^}]+)\}|([^{}]+)/ (same idiom as the vulnerable extract regex)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it scans the same url string as extractUrlVariableNames; the vulnerable variant is a one-character difference from the existing safe pattern

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a preview-name normaliser regex like /[\w-]+-preview/ on mediaType.previews
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: merge already strips '-preview' from each preview string on the /graphql path

O10_build.toolchain: Node >= 18, npm, esbuild + tsc build, vitest tests
O10_build.project_tests: test/parse.test.ts (endpoint.parse), plus test/endpoint.test.ts and others under test/; vitest run --coverage

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a lookbehind or length cap only to the accept-header preview regex at src/parse.ts:62 and leave the URL-variable regexes alone.

out_of_scope_notes: The other regexes in src/ (src/parse.ts:17, src/parse.ts:52, src/util/url-template.ts:33, src/util/url-template.ts:160, src/util/url-template.ts:172) read as linear on inspection; no uncovered ReDoS route found.

Linearity of the remaining regexes judged by reading only; not benchmarked.
